source: Shem Tov Hebrew Matthew (Even Bochan, Ibn Shaprut c. 1385; critical text ed. G. Howard, base ms British Library Add. 26964)

verses.translation: And it came to pass{H1961}, when Yeshua{H3442} went out{H3318} of the Sanctuary{H4720}, as he was walking{H1980}, his disciples{H8527} approached{H5066} to show{H7200} him the buildings{H1146} of the Sanctuary{H4720}.

one_way_hebrew: Uses מקדש (mikdash, H4720) — the Torah word for the holy precinct (Exod 25:8) — where Greek has ἱερόν. A Hebrew author writes מקדש naturally; a back-translator from Greek tends toward בית המקדש throughout, but this text varies between מקדש (here) and בית המקדש (v. 3) exactly as living Hebrew does.
תלמידיו (talmidav, H8527) — talmid is the native rabbinic-Hebrew word for a disciple (1 Chr 25:8), not a calque of Greek μαθητής.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק ק׳ (Perek 100) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (24:1): ms G reads בנין הבית והמקדש for בניני המקדש, and adds את before המקדש; G also reads להראותו with the direct object.

verses.translation: And he said{H559}: Do you see{H7200} all{H3605} these{H428}? Amen{H543}, I say{H559} to you that everything{H3605} will be torn down{H2040}, and there will not remain{H7604} there{H8033} a stone{H68} upon a stone{H68}.

one_way_hebrew: אמן אני אומר לכם — the Hebrew retains אמן (amen, H543), the untranslated Hebrew word the Greek text itself preserves as ἀμήν. In Hebrew it needs no explanation; in Greek it is a foreign loanword.
יהרס (H2040) — the verb of Exod 19:21,24 and Jer 1:10 for divine tearing-down.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:2): שם omitted in A; EF read ואומר for ויאמר and G adds להם ('to them').

verses.translation: And as he sat{H3427} on the Mount{H2022} of the Olives{H2132}, opposite{H5048} the house{H1004} of the Sanctuary{H4720}, Petros and Yochanan{H3110} and Andreah asked{H7592} him in secret{H5643}: When{H4970} will all{H3605} these{H428} be, and what is the sign{H226} that will be when all these matters{H6045} come, or when they will begin{H2490}, and when will be the end{H8503} of the world{H5769} and your coming{H935}?

greek_deviations: The Hebrew names the questioners — Petros, Yochanan, and Andreah — where Greek Matthew has only 'the disciples came to him privately.' Mark 13:3 names Peter, James, John, and Andrew 'opposite the temple' (κατέναντι τοῦ ἱεροῦ); the Hebrew Matthew shares Mark's scene, including נגד בית המקדש ('opposite the house of the Sanctuary'), which Greek Matthew lacks entirely.
The question is fuller than the Greek: 'when will these matters come, or when will they begin' — a two-stage question (onset and completion) absent from the Greek.
translation_notes: בסתר — 'in secret' (Sepharad: 'in confidence'). The scan of Howard's text reads בסתר; the circulating transcription's מסתר is a typo, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:3): פיטרוש] פיטרו AG; אנדריאה] אנדראוס G, אנדריאש EF; שאלו] שאל A; ABEF omit בית; A reads וביאתה; F ומתי for מתי.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} answered{H6030} them: Take heed{H8104} lest{H6435} a man{H376} lead you astray{H8582}.

one_way_hebrew: יתעה (H8582, ta'ah) — the shepherd-word for straying sheep (Ps 119:176; Isa 53:6). The whole discourse turns on this root: the deceivers make the flock wander.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:4): לכם] אתכם EF; השמרו] + לכם EF.

verses.translation: For many{H7227} will come{H935} in my name{H8034}, saying{H559}: I am he, the Mashiach{H4899} — and they will lead you astray{H8582}.

one_way_hebrew: בשמי (H8034) — 'in my Name.' The Hebrew reader hears the full weight of שם, the Name as identity and authority; see the same idiom of prophets speaking בשם יהוה (Deut 18:22).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:5): הוא omitted in A; A reads אתכם for את הרבים.

verses.translation: And you, when you hear{H8085} the wars{H4421} and the company{H2267} of armies{H6635}, take heed{H8104} lest{H6435} you be terrified{H926}; for all this is destined{H6264} to come{H935} — but the end{H8503} is not yet.

one_way_hebrew: צבאות (H6635) — 'hosts, armies,' the word of יהוה צבאות. Greek has ἀκοὰς πολέμων ('rumors of wars'); the Hebrew is concrete: the mustering of hosts.
תכלית (H8503) — Job's word for the utter end/limit (Job 26:10; 28:3). The discourse consistently uses תכלית where Greek has τέλος.
translation_notes: תהבלו — the printed text has תהבלו (as if from הבל); ms G reads תבהלו from בהל (H926, 'be terrified, dismayed'), which the sense requires and all translators follow. The consonants differ only by letter order.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:6): תהבלו] תבהלו G.

verses.translation: And nation{H1471} will rise{H6965} against nation{H1471}, and kingdom{H4467} against kingdom{H4467}; and there will be many{H7227} tumults{H4103}, and heavy{H3515} famine{H7458}, and quaking{H7494} in places{H4725}.

one_way_hebrew: מהומות (H4103, mehumah) — the covenant-curse word: 'the LORD shall send upon thee cursing, tumult (המהומה)' (Deut 28:20; cf. 1 Sam 5:9; Zech 14:13). Greek has no equivalent term here.
רעב כבד — 'heavy famine,' the exact idiom of Gen 12:10; 41:31 (כבד הרעב). Greek λιμοί is bare 'famines.'

verses.translation: All{H3605} these{H428} are the beginning{H8462} of the pains{H4341}.

one_way_hebrew: מכאובות (H4341, mak'ov) — the word of Isa 53:3-4, the man of pains who carried our pains, and of Lam 1:12. Greek ὠδίνων ('birth-pangs') narrows it; the Hebrew word carries the Suffering-Servant echo.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:8): המכאובות omitted in A.

verses.translation: Then{H227} they will bind{H631} you for afflictions{H6869} and will kill{H2026} you, and you will be a reproach{H2781} to all{H3605} the peoples{H5971} on account of my name{H8034}.

one_way_hebrew: חרפה (H2781) — 'reproach,' the Psalter's word for the righteous sufferer (Ps 22:7; 69:8-10). Greek μισούμενοι ('hated') loses the scriptural echo.

יאסרו (H631) — 'bind, imprison' (Gen 42:24; Judg 16:21); Greek has παραδώσουσιν ('hand over'). Mss AEF read ימסרו ('deliver over'), assimilating toward the Greek — the harder reading יאסרו stands in the base text.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:9): יאסרו] ימסרו AEF.

verses.translation: And then{H227} many{H7227} will be agitated{H7264}, and will betray{H898} one another, and will be enraged{H7107} among themselves{H996}.

one_way_hebrew: בגד (H898) — the covenant word for treachery (Mal 2:10-16, 'why do we deal treacherously every man against his brother?'). Greek παραδώσουσιν ('hand over') is procedural; the Hebrew is relational treachery.
קצף (H7107) — divine-and-human wrath word (Gen 41:10; Isa 47:6).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:10): ירגזו] ירגשו EF; בהם] באים BF; ויתקצפו] ויתקפצו F.

verses.translation: And prophets{H5030} of falsehood{H8267} will arise{H6965} and will lead astray{H8582} the many{H7227}.

one_way_hebrew: נביאי השקר — 'prophets of the lie,' Jeremiah's exact phrase (Jer 23:26, נביאי השקר; cf. Jer 27:15 'they prophesy falsely — לשקר — in my name'). Greek ψευδοπροφῆται is a single compound; the Hebrew is Jeremiah's living construct phrase.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:11): השקר] שקר G.

verses.translation: And when wickedness{H7564} multiplies{H7235}, the love{H160} of many{H7227} will grow numb{H6313}.

one_way_hebrew: תפוג (H6313, pug) — 'grow numb, faint': Jacob's heart 'fainted' (ויפג לבו, Gen 45:26); 'the law is slacked' (תפוג תורה, Hab 1:4). Greek ψυγήσεται ('grow cold') is a thermal metaphor; the Hebrew is the scriptural numbing of the heart — and Hab 1:4 pairs it with lawlessness exactly as here.

verses.translation: And whoever waits{H2442} until{H5704} the end{H8503} will be saved{H3467}.

one_way_hebrew: יחכה (H2442, chakah) — 'wait expectantly': 'blessed are all they that wait for him' (Isa 30:18); 'though it tarry, wait for it' (Hab 2:3). Greek ὑπομείνας ('endures') is passive holding-out; the Hebrew is active expectant waiting — the same verb the prophets use for waiting on YHWH.
יושע (H3467, yasha) — the root of the name ישו״ע: whoever waits to the end will be saved, and the Savior's own name carries the promise.

verses.translation: And this good-news{H1309} — in the foreign tongue{H3937}, evangeli — will be proclaimed{H1875} in all{H3605} the earth{H776} for a testimony{H5715} concerning me to all the nations{H1471}, and then{H227} the end{H8503} will come{H935}.

one_way_hebrew: בשורה (H1309) — the herald's good report (2 Sam 18:20-27; Isa 52:7), exactly as in Mark 1:1 on this site. The text then glosses it לעז אוו״נגילי — 'in the foreign tongue, evangeli' — a scribal gloss giving the Latin/Greek loanword for Hebrew readers. A translator FROM Greek would have started from εὐαγγέλιον and never needed to gloss his own source-word; the gloss runs the other way: the Hebrew word is native, the Greek word is the foreign visitor.
ותדרש (H1875, darash) — 'will be sought/expounded' — the rabbinic word for expounding Scripture (whence midrash). Greek κηρυχθήσεται ('heralded') flattens it.
greek_deviations: לעדות עלי — 'for a testimony concerning ME' — where Greek has 'for a testimony to all the nations' without 'concerning me.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:14): בכל] + אפסי ABEFG ('to the ends of all the earth', echoing Isa 52:10); אוונגילי] אונגילי A, אואנגילי EF; לעז] בלעז B; על omitted in A; תבא] בא G.
The transcription's footnote 131 confirms: eujaggelion = Latin evangelium.

verses.translation: This is Antichristos, and this is the abomination{H8251} that desolates{H8074} spoken{H559} by the mouth{H6310} of Daniel{H1840}, standing{H5975} in the holy{H6918} place{H4725} — and let the reader{H7121} understand{H995}.

one_way_hebrew: שקוץ שומם — the exact consonants of Dan 12:11 (שקוץ שמם) and Dan 11:31. The Hebrew text quotes Daniel in Daniel's own words; Greek βδέλυγμα τῆς ἐρημώσεως is a translation of them.
על פי דניאל — 'by the mouth of Daniel,' the Hebrew citation idiom (עַל־פִּי, Exod 17:1).
greek_deviations: The text opens with a gloss absent from the Greek: זה אנטיק״ריסטוש — 'this is Antichristos' — identifying the abomination with the Antichrist by name (a Greek loanword written into the Hebrew text, marked as foreign by the scribal gershayim). Like the evangeli gloss in v. 14, it shows a Hebrew text being annotated for readers who knew the church's Greek-Latin vocabulary.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:15): זה] זהו EF, והוא A; AG add בדניאל הנביא ('in Daniel the prophet'); A reads אנטיקריסט.

verses.translation: Then{H227} let those who are in Yehudah{H3063} flee{H5127} to the mountains{H2022}.

one_way_hebrew: ינוסו להרים — the flight-to-the-mountains command of Gen 19:17 (ההרה המלט) and the psalmist's נודו הרכם (Ps 11:1).
textual_notes: ביודא — the ms spells Yehudah defectively (יודא, an Aramaic-type form); ms G normalizes to ביהודה. The transcription's footnote asks whether it is a typo for ביודה; Howard prints ביודא.
Howard's apparatus (24:16): ואז] אז AEF.

verses.translation: And he who is on the house{H1004}, let him not go down{H3381} to take any thing{H1697} from his house{H1004}.

translation_notes: לקרות — an odd form in the base ms; mss AB read לקחת ('to take', H3947), G לקח, EF omit. The sense 'to take' is followed by all translators.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:17): לקרות] לקחת AB, לקח G, omit EF.

verses.translation: And he who is in the field{H7704}, let him not return{H7725} to take{H3947} his tunic{H3801}.

one_way_hebrew: כתנתו (H3801, kethoneth) — the garment word of Gen 3:21 (the coats God made) and Gen 37:3 (Joseph's tunic). Greek ἱμάτιον is generic 'cloak.'

verses.translation: Woe{H1945} to the pregnant{H2030} and to the nursing{H3243} in those{H1992} days{H3117}!

one_way_hebrew: הוי (H1945) — the prophetic woe-cry (Isa 5:8ff; Amos 5:18). Greek οὐαί is itself a transliteration of this Hebrew interjection.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:19): הוי] הוא EF.

verses.translation: Pray{H6419} to El{H410} that your flight{H4498} will not be in the winter{H5638} or on the Shabbat{H7676}.

one_way_hebrew: מנוסה (H4498) — the covenant-curse flight word (Lev 26:36, 'they shall flee as fleeing from a sword'). Greek φυγή occurs only here in the NT.
בסתו — סְתָו is the Song of Songs' word for the rainy season ('the winter is past', Song 2:11), the only place it occurs in Scripture. A Hebrew author reaches for it naturally.
The Shabbat clause stands in the Hebrew exactly as in Greek Matthew — and in no other gospel: the community addressed keeps the Shabbat.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:20): לאל omitted in G; בסתו] בסתיו A; mss BEFH read ביום השבת ('on the day of the Shabbat'); A reads ושבת.

verses.translation: For then{H227} there will be great{H1419} distress{H6869} which has not been{H1961} from the creation{H1254} of the world{H5769} until now{H6258}, and like it{H3644} there will not be again.

one_way_hebrew: צרה גדולה... אשר לא נהיתה — the Hebrew tracks Dan 12:1 (והיתה עת צרה אשר לא נהיתה מהיות גוי) word-for-word in its key terms: צרה and לא נהיתה. The Greek θλῖψις μεγάλη translates; the Hebrew shares Daniel's own vocabulary.
מבראת העולם — from ברא (H1254), the creation verb of Gen 1:1, where Greek has ἀπ' ἀρχῆς κόσμου ('from the beginning of the world').
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:21): אשר לא] שלא F.

verses.translation: And were it not{H3884} that those{H1992} days{H3117} are few{H4592}, no flesh{H1320} would be saved{H3467}; but for the sake{H5668} of the chosen{H977}, those days will be made few{H4591}.

one_way_hebrew: כל בשר — 'all flesh,' the flood-narrative phrase (Gen 6:12-13); it anticipates the Noah comparison of vv. 37-39.
הנבחרים (H977, bachar) — 'the chosen,' the election verb of Deut 7:6-7.
greek_deviations: The Hebrew says the days will be made FEW (מעטים / ימעטו, H4592/H4591), not 'shortened' (Greek κολοβωθήσονται, 'cut off, amputated'). Few days and amputated days are different pictures: the Hebrew counts them; the Greek cuts them.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:22): יושיע] יושע ABEFG ('would be saved'); ולולי] ולילא A; second ההם omitted in EF.

verses.translation: And in that{H1931} time{H2165}, if a man{H376} says{H559} to you: Behold{H2009}, the Mashiach{H4899} is here — or there{H8033} — do not believe{H539} it.

one_way_hebrew: זמן (H2165) — the late-Biblical Hebrew time word (Esth 9:27,31; Neh 2:6), natural to a Hebrew author of this register.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:23): המשיח omitted in G; ABEF add לכאן ('here') after או לשם.

verses.translation: For anointed-ones{H4899} of lies{H8267} and prophets{H5030} of falsehood{H8267} will arise{H6965}, and they will give{H5414} great{H1419} signs{H226} and wonders{H4159}, in such manner that — if it were possible{H3201} — they would bring the chosen{H977} into error{H8582}.

one_way_hebrew: אותות ומופתים (H226, H4159) — 'signs and wonders,' the fixed Torah pair (Deut 13:2-3!). Deut 13 is the very law being invoked: the false prophet whose sign comes true, sent to test whether Israel will be led astray. The Hebrew reader hears the statute; the Greek σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα is its translation.
משיחי שקרים — 'false anointed ones,' built like נביאי השקר, both construct chains from שקר (H8267), Jeremiah's word.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:24): שקרים] רבים G; יבאו] יביאו A.
The printed text reads ונבאי (defective); the transcription's footnote notes it should be נביאי — same word, plene spelling.

verses.translation: Behold{H2009}, I am telling{H559} it to you before{H6924} it comes to be{H1961}.

one_way_hebrew: הנני — the prophetic 'here am I / behold me' formula; and the sentence is Isaiah's argument from foretelling: 'before it came to pass I announced it to you' (Isa 48:5, בטרם תבוא השמעתיך).
textual_notes: In Shem Tov, verse 25 stands AFTER verse 26 — the announcement seals the double warning. Howard's apparatus (24:25): 'Vs 25 comes after vs 26 in Shem-Tob'; היותו omitted in A. The verses are given here in numerical order for the reader's convenience; the ms reading order is 24, 26, 25, 27.

verses.translation: And if they say{H559} to you: Behold, he is in the wilderness{H4057} — do not go out{H3318}; and: Behold, he is in the chambers{H2315} — do not believe{H539} it.

one_way_hebrew: בחדרים (H2315, cheder) — 'inner chambers,' the hiding place of Isa 26:20 ('enter into thy chambers... hide thyself'). Greek ταμείοις translates the same picture.
textual_notes: This verse precedes v. 25 in the ms (see note there). Howard's apparatus (24:26): ואם] ואז A; תצאו] תשאלו EF; והנו] הנו A.

verses.translation: Again{H5750} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}: Just as the lightning{H1300} goes out{H3318} in the east{H4217} and is seen{H7200} in the west{H4628}, so will be the coming{H935} of the Son{H1121} of Man{H120}.

one_way_hebrew: ברק (H1300) — the theophany lightning (Exod 19:16; Ps 97:4). בן האדם (H1121, H120) — Ezekiel's title (ben adam, 93x) and Dan 7:13's בר אנש; in Hebrew it is a native idiom, in Greek an awkward calque (ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου).
textual_notes: Shem Tov's section heading פרק ק״א (Perek 101) begins here, marking vv. 27-36 as one unit: the lightning, the carcass, the darkened lights, the ingathering, the fig tree, the passing of heaven and earth, and the unknown day — one discourse.
Howard's apparatus (24:27): להם omitted in A; במזרח] ממזרח BG; שלבן] של בן AEF.

verses.translation: In whatever place{H4725} the carcass{H1472} is, there{H8033} the eagles{H5404} will join together{H2266}.

one_way_hebrew: גויה (H1472) — 'carcass, body': Samson's lion (Judg 14:8-9), where the swarm gathers IN the carcass — the same picture. Greek πτῶμα translates it.
נשר (H5404) — the nesher of Job 39:30 ('where the slain are, there is she'), which this saying quotes in substance. The Hebrew proverb closes the loop to Job; the Greek ἀετοί merely translates.
translation_notes: יתחברו (H2266, chavar) — 'join themselves together, assemble as companions' — the same root as חברת הצבאות in v. 6.

verses.translation: And in that{H1931} hour{H8160}, after{H310} those{H1992} days{H3117}, the sun{H8121} will be darkened{H2821}, and the moon{H3394} will not beam forth{H5050} its light{H216}, and the stars{H3556} will fall{H5307} from the heavens{H8064}, and the host{H2428} of the heavens{H8064} will be shaken{H5110}.

one_way_hebrew: והירח לא יגיה אורו — Isa 13:10's oracle against Babylon verbatim: וירח לא יגיה אורו ('and the moon shall not cause her light to shine'). The verb נגה (H5050) and the whole clause are Isaiah's own consonants. Greek Matthew (ἡ σελήνη οὐ δώσει τὸ φέγγος αὐτῆς) translates Isaiah; the Hebrew Matthew QUOTES him. A back-translator from Greek would have to reconstruct Isaiah's exact wording by accident.

חיל השמים — 'the host of heaven' as an army (חיל, H2428); cf. צבא השמים of Isa 34:4 which 'rots away' as its stars fall like leaves — the same double scene (host shaken, stars falling) stands behind both clauses.
greek_deviations: THE BASE TEXT HAS NO TRIBULATION HERE. It reads: 'And in that hour, AFTER THOSE DAYS, the sun will be darkened...' — where Greek Matthew reads 'Immediately after the tribulation of those days.' No 'immediately,' no 'tribulation': the darkening follows 'those days' themselves. Howard's apparatus: mss ABEFG add צרת ('the tribulation of') before הימים — the majority of late mss assimilate to the Greek, but the base text (British Library Add. 26964) stands without it, and Howard prints the add in parentheses in his English: 'after (the tribulation of) those days.'
בשעה — 'in that HOUR': the Hebrew binds the celestial darkening to a definite hour after those days, a sharper time-marker than the Greek's εὐθέως ('immediately').
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:29): אחרי] + צרת ABEFG; מהשמים] מן השמים EF.

verses.translation: And then{H227} the sign{H226} of the Son{H1121} of Man{H120} will appear{H7200} in the heavens{H8064}, and all{H3605} the families{H4940} of the earth{H127} will weep{H1058}, and they will see{H7200} the Son of Man in the thick clouds{H5645} of the heavens{H8064} with a great{H7227} host{H2428} and with a dreadful{H3372} appearance{H6699}.

one_way_hebrew: משפחות האדמה — 'the families of the ground/earth': the exact phrase of Gen 12:3 and Amos 3:2 (משפחות האדמה). Greek has φυλαὶ τῆς γῆς ('tribes of the earth', from Zech 12:12 LXX); the Hebrew stands on the Abrahamic-covenant phrase — the same families to be blessed in Abraham's seed now weep at his coming.

בעבי השמים — עב (H5645), the thick storm-cloud of theophany: 'YHWH rides upon a swift cloud (עב)' (Isa 19:1); 'thick clouds of the skies' (עבי שחקים, Ps 18:12 = 2 Sam 22:12). Dan 7:13 has ענני שמיא; this text's עבי is the heavier storm-word.
greek_deviations: בחיל רב ובצורה נוראה — 'with a great HOST and a DREADFUL APPEARANCE' — where Greek reads 'with power and great glory.' The Hebrew pictures an army (חיל, as in v. 29's host of heaven) and a fearsome form (נורא, the word of Exod 15:11, 'fearful in praises'); no 'glory' (כבוד) appears.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:30): שלבן] של בן A.

verses.translation: And he will send{H7971} his messengers{H4397} with a shofar{H7782} and with a great{H1419} voice{H6963}, to gather{H622} his chosen{H977} from the four{H702} winds{H7307} of the heavens{H8064}, from the end{H7097} of the heavens unto their ends{H7098}.

one_way_hebrew: בשופר ובקול גדול — 'with a shofar and a great voice': Sinai's pairing exactly (Exod 19:16,19 — קול שופר; Isa 27:13, 'the great shofar shall be blown... and they shall come which were ready to perish'). Isa 27:13 is the ingathering-by-shofar prophecy this verse enacts. Greek 'with a great trumpet-sound' merges the pair.

מארבע רוחות השמים — 'from the four winds of the heavens': Zech 2:10 ('I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heavens') and Ezek 37:9 — the regathering wind. The words are the prophets' own.

מקצה השמים עד קצותם — Deut 30:4's regathering promise ('if any of thine be driven out unto the outmost parts of heaven, from thence will YHWH thy God gather thee') fused with Ps 19:7 (מקצה השמים... על קצותם). The verse is a mosaic of the ingathering texts; only in Hebrew are the tesserae visible.
מלאכיו (H4397) — 'his messengers/sent-ones': the same word serves for the sent ones of v. 34's harvest (cf. Matt 13:41) and for the angels; Hebrew does not split 'messenger' from 'angel.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:31): ובקול omitted in E; the first השמים omitted in AEF; ועד] עד EF.

verses.translation: From the fig{H8384} tree{H6086} learn{H3925} the parable{H4912}: when you see{H7200} its branches{H6057} and leaves{H5929} sprouting{H6779}, you know{H3045} that —

one_way_hebrew: משל (H4912) — mashal, the native Hebrew category of parable/proverb (Prov 1:1; Ezek 17:2's tree-mashal). Greek παραβολή translates it.
ענף, עלה, צמח (H6057, H5929, H6779) — branch, leaf, sprout: the vocabulary of Ezek 17's cedar parable and Gen 40:10.
textual_notes: The sentence runs over the verse-break into v. 33 ('...that near is he to the gates'). Howard's apparatus notes at 24:32: all mss jump from קרוב of v. 32 to קרוב of v. 33 (haplography) — the mss lost the words between the two occurrences of קרוב, so vv. 32-33 survive as one continuous sentence.
The scan reads ענפיה ('its branches'); the circulating transcription's אנפיה is a typo, corrected here.

verses.translation: — near{H7138} is he, at the gates{H8179}.

greek_deviations: לשערים — 'at the GATES' (שערים, H8179, the city-gate word of judgment and rule, Deut 16:18; Ps 24:7 'lift up your heads, O ye gates... and the King of glory shall come in'). Greek has ἐπὶ θύραις ('at the doors'). A gate is where the king enters and where court is held; a door is domestic. The Hebrew says the King is near the gates.
translation_notes: הוא — 'HE is near': the Hebrew has a personal subject (the Son of Man), where the Greek ἐγγύς ἐστιν can be read 'it is near' (the summer/the end). The Hebrew removes the ambiguity: he is near, at the gates.
textual_notes: See v. 32 note: Howard's apparatus records that all mss jump from קרוב (v. 32) to קרוב (v. 33) — Howard's English attaches 'near' to v. 32 and leaves v. 33 as 'to the gates'; the transcription's footnote 138 notes קרוב belongs with v. 33.

verses.translation: Amen{H543}, I say{H559} to you that this{H2088} generation{H1755} will not pass away{H5674} until{H5704} all{H3605} these{H428} things{H1697} are done{H6213}.

one_way_hebrew: דור (H1755) — the flood-generation word (Gen 7:1, 'in this generation'); the discourse is about to turn to the days of Noah (v. 37), and the Hebrew reader hears דור המבול behind זה הדור.
יהיו עשוים — 'shall be DONE' (עשה, H6213), the doing-word of creation and command, where Greek has γένηται ('happen').
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:34): עשוים] נעשים H; אלו הדברים] הדברים האלו H; אלו omitted in B.

verses.translation: And the heavens{H8064} and the earth{H776} will pass away{H5674}.

one_way_hebrew: יעברו (H5674) — the same verb as v. 34's 'this generation shall not pass': the Hebrew sets דור and שמים וארץ in deliberate contrast with one verb; Greek uses παρέρχομαι for both, but only the Hebrew reader sees the shared root carry the a-fortiori: the generation outlasts nothing, the heavens themselves pass.
greek_deviations: THE VERSE ENDS HERE. Shem Tov's text reads only 'And the heavens and the earth will pass away' — it does NOT contain 'but my words shall not pass away.' Greek Matthew, Greek Mark (13:31), Luke 21:33, and the Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew all carry the second clause; the Shem Tov ms family carries none of it, in any of Howard's nine mss (no variant is recorded). Read with v. 36, the sentence serves a different function here: it states the event ('heaven and earth WILL pass away'), and v. 36 dates the knowledge of it.

verses.translation: And from{H4480} that{H1931} day{H3117} and from that time{H6256}, there is none{H369} who knows{H3045} — not even the messengers{H4397} of the heavens{H8064} — except the Father{H1} alone{H905}.

greek_deviations: NO 'NEITHER THE SON.' The Shem Tov text reads: 'not even the messengers of the heavens, except the Father alone' — with no οὐδὲ ὁ υἱός clause. The 'neither the Son' reading of א* B D in Greek Matthew is absent from the entire Shem Tov ms family (Howard records no variant adding it).

The Hebrew opens ומהיום ההוא ומהעת ההיא — 'and FROM that day and FROM that time' (the preposition מן, 'from') — not 'concerning (περὶ) that day.' Following directly on v. 35 ('the heavens and the earth will pass away'), the plain construal is temporal: from the day heaven and earth pass, from that time onward, no one knows — none but the Father. Greek's περὶ δὲ τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης ('but concerning that day') re-points the sentence at the calendar question; the Hebrew's מן points at what lies beyond the passing of heaven and earth. Howard's English ('But of that day or that time') follows the Greek construal against his own text's preposition.
translation_notes: עת (H6256) — 'time, season' (Eccl 3:1); the pair יום/עת answers the disciples' double question of v. 3 (when will it be / when will it begin).
מלאכי השמים — 'the messengers of the heavens' (H4397): Hebrew מלאך means a sent one; the same word served for the gathering messengers of v. 31.
textual_notes: No variants recorded in Howard's apparatus for this verse — the reading is uniform across the Shem Tov mss.

verses.translation: Again{H5750} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}: As in the days{H3117} of Noach{H5146}, so will it be in the days{H3117} of the Son{H1121} of Man{H120}.

one_way_hebrew: The days-of-Noach / days-of-the-Son-of-Man symmetry rests on יום (H3117) both times; Greek breaks the symmetry with ἡμέραι... παρουσία.
greek_deviations: 'In the DAYS of the Son of Man' — Greek Matthew reads 'so shall the παρουσία (coming) of the Son of Man be,' but the Hebrew reads בימינו של בן האדם, 'in the days of the Son of Man' — exactly LUKE's wording (Luke 17:26, 'as it was in the days of Noah, so shall it be also in the days of the Son of Man'). The Hebrew Matthew and Luke agree on 'days' against Greek Matthew's 'parousia'; days are a span, a parousia is an arrival. Mss ABEF read ביאתו ('his coming'), assimilating to the Greek — the base text stands with Luke.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's section heading פרק ק״ב (Perek 102) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (24:37): בימינו] ביאתו ABEF.

verses.translation: As they were before{H6924} the flood{H3999} — eating{H398} and drinking{H8354} and being fruitful{H6509} and multiplying{H7235} — until the day{H3117} that Noach{H5146} entered{H935} the ark{H8392}.

one_way_hebrew: ופרים ורבים — 'being fruitful and multiplying': Gen 1:28's own blessing (פרו ורבו), which the flood generation went on performing while ignoring the builder of the ark. Greek Matthew has 'marrying and giving in marriage' (γαμοῦντες καὶ γαμίζοντες); the Hebrew reaches instead for the Genesis creation-mandate — a specifically Hebrew irony no Greek translator would invent.
מבול (H3999) and תיבה (H8392) — the flood and the ark by their Genesis names (Gen 6:14; 7:6). Greek κιβωτός translates תיבה.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:38): ופרים] פרים A.

verses.translation: And they did not know{H3045} until the flood{H3999} came{H935} upon them and destroyed them{H7843}; so will be the coming{H935} of the Son{H1121} of Man{H120}.

one_way_hebrew: וישחיתם (H7843, shachat) — 'destroyed them': the flood narrative's own verb (Gen 6:13,17, 'I will destroy them with the earth... to destroy all flesh'). Greek ἦρεν ('swept away') loses Genesis's word.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:39): המבול] מבול EF.

verses.translation: Then{H227} if there are two{H8147} plowing{H2790} in one field{H7704} — the one righteous{H6662} and the other wicked{H7563} — the one will be captured{H3920} and the other left{H5800}.

greek_deviations: The Hebrew adds what the Greek leaves unsaid: 'the one RIGHTEOUS and the other WICKED' (צדיק/רשע — the fixed pair of Gen 18:23; Mal 3:18). The Greek's bare 'one is taken and one is left' has bred endless debate over which one fares better; the Hebrew text answers inside the verse.
translation_notes: ילכד (H3920, lakad) — 'be caught, captured' (as in a snare, Ps 9:16; Jer 5:26; cf. Luke 21:35, 'as a snare shall it come'). In every scriptural use, being 'taken' (נלכד) is the fate of the judged, not a rescue: read with the addition righteous/wicked, it is the wicked who is captured and the righteous who is left standing — as in the days of Noach, when the flood 'took them all away' and Noach was left.
The scan reads והאחר ('and the other') at the last clause; earlier clauses use והאחד.

verses.translation: Two{H8147} women{H802} grinding{H2912} at one mill{H2911} — the one will be captured{H3920} and the other left{H5800}. And this will be because the messengers{H4397}, at the end{H8503} of the world{H5769}, will remove{H5493} the stumbling-blocks{H4383} from the world and will separate{H6504} the good{H2896} from the evil{H7451}.

one_way_hebrew: טוחנות בטחון — grinding (H2912) at the mill (טחון, H2911, Lam 5:13's word); the pair is native Hebrew assonance.
מכשול (H4383) — 'stumbling-block,' Ezekiel's word (מכשול עונם, Ezek 7:19; 14:3-4); Greek σκάνδαλον translates it.
greek_deviations: The verse carries an explanation absent from the Greek: 'this will be because the messengers at the end of the world will remove the stumbling-blocks from the world and separate the good from the evil.' It is Matthew 13:41's harvest-explanation ('the Son of Man shall send forth his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all the stumbling-blocks — πάντα τὰ σκάνδαλα') stitched into the Olivet discourse. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew carries the same sentence — a shared family reading against the Greek. It settles the 'taken or left?' question the same way v. 40 does: what is removed is the stumbling-block.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:41): שתים] וב׳ EF, וב׳ אחד G; מהעולם] מן העולם A.

verses.translation: Then{H227} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}: Therefore watch{H8104} with me{H5973}, because you do not know{H3045} what hour{H8160} your master{H113} comes{H935}.

greek_deviations: שמרו עמי — 'watch WITH ME' — absent from the Greek ('watch therefore'). The same Hebrew consonants עמי also read 'my people' (ammi): 'watch, my people.' Both readings stand in the unpointed text; Howard translates 'watch with me.' Either way the verse binds the watchers to the speaker in a way the Greek does not.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's section heading פרק ק״ג (Perek 103) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (24:42): שמרו] שמעו G ('hear'); G transposes אדוניכם בא.

verses.translation: This{H2063} you know{H3045}: if one had known{H3045} what hour{H8160} the thief{H1590} comes{H935}, he would watch{H8104} and not allow{H5800} him to break into{H2266} his house{H1004}.

one_way_hebrew: The ABEFG reading לחתור (H2864, chatar) — 'to dig through' — is Job's word for the thief: 'in the dark they dig through houses' (חתר בחשך בתים, Job 24:16; cf. Ezek 8:8). Greek διορυγῆναι ('be dug through') translates precisely this Hebrew idiom of burglary through mud-brick walls.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:43): לחבור] לחתור ABEFG — the base ms reads לחבור ('to join/attach to'), the majority לחתור ('to dig through'), which Howard accepts for his English '(to dig) into his house.'
Howard's apparatus (24:43): יבא] בא A; ידע] + אדון הבית A ('the master of the house').

verses.translation: So{H3651} you also, be ready{H3559}, for you do not know{H3045} what hour{H8160} the Son{H1121} of Man{H120} is destined{H6264} to come{H935}.

one_way_hebrew: נכונים (H3559, kun) — 'be established, ready': Sinai's preparation word ('be ready against the third day', Exod 19:11,15). The waiting community is put under Sinai's readiness command.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:44): עתיד לבא] בא BG; האדם] אדם FG; תהיו] היו EF.

verses.translation: What{H4100} do you think{H2803} of the faithful{H539} and wise{H2450} servant{H5650} whom his master{H113} placed{H7760} over his little ones{H2945}, to give{H5414} their food{H400} in its season{H6256}?

one_way_hebrew: לתת אכלם בעתו — 'to give their food in its season': the Psalter's providence formula verbatim (Ps 104:27, לתת אכלם בעתו; Ps 145:15). The steward is written into God's own feeding role by direct quotation; Greek ('to give them food in due season') translates the psalm without knowing it.

טפיו (H2945, taf) — 'his LITTLE ONES': the covenant word for the children of the household (Gen 47:12, 'Joseph nourished... according to their little ones'; Exod 10:10). Greek Matthew has οἰκετείας ('household staff'). The master sets the servant over children, not staff — and v. 47 escalates it.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:45): והחכם omitted in G; לתת] + להם A.

verses.translation: Happy{H835} is that servant{H5650} whom his master{H113}, when he comes{H935}, finds doing{H6213} so.

one_way_hebrew: אשרי (H835) — the Psalter's beatitude-word (Ps 1:1). The Greek μακάριος renders the same Hebrew form that opens the Psalms.
translation_notes: The base ms reads שתצווהו ('whom his master shall command'); mss ABEF read שימצאהו ('whom his master shall FIND'), matching the Greek εὑρήσει, and Howard's English follows the variant: 'whose lord (finds) him doing thus.' The translation above follows the sense with the variant noted.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:46): שתצווהו] שימצאהו ABEF.

verses.translation: Amen{H543}, I say{H559} to you that he will set him{H7760} over his little ones{H2945}.

greek_deviations: Greek Matthew promises the servant rule 'over all his GOODS' (ὑπάρχουσιν); the Hebrew base text promises him the master's LITTLE ONES (טפיו) — the reward of faithfulness over children is more children, not property. Mss ABEFG read טובו ('his goods'), assimilating to the Greek; the base text stands apart.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:47): טפיו] טובו ABEFG.

verses.translation: But if that servant{H5650} is evil{H7451}, and says{H559} in his heart{H3820}: My master{H113} delays{H4102} in coming{H935} —

one_way_hebrew: מתמהמה (H4102, mahah) — the hithpalpel 'lingering' of Gen 19:16 (Lot lingered) and Hab 2:3 ('though it tarry — יתמהמה — wait for it'). Hab 2:3 is the exact counter-text: the vision tarries, the faithful wait, the wicked servant stops waiting. The Greek χρονίζει cannot carry the allusion.
ויאמר בלבו — 'says in his heart,' the fool's inward speech formula (Ps 14:1; Deut 8:17).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:48): ובא] לבא AEF, לבוא B; העבד] העב A.

verses.translation: and begins{H2490} to beat{H5221} the servants{H5650} of his master{H113}, and eats{H398} and drinks{H8354} with the gluttons{H2151} —

one_way_hebrew: הזוללים (H2151, zolel) — Proverbs' gluttons: 'be not among winebibbers, among gluttonous eaters of flesh' (Prov 23:20-21), where the glutton's end is poverty and shame; and the rebellious son of Deut 21:20 is זולל וסבא. Greek has 'eats and drinks with the DRUNKARDS' (μεθυόντων); the Hebrew names the זולל — the Torah's own category for the son who will not hear.
translation_notes: עבדו אדוניו — the printed text has singular עבדו with אדוניו ('the servant(s) of his master'); Howard renders 'the servant of his lord.' The idiom is elliptical; the plural sense of the Greek (συνδούλους, fellow-servants) is not in the Hebrew.

verses.translation: then his master{H113} will come{H935} in a day{H3117} he does not await{H2442} and in a time{H6256} he does not know{H3045},

one_way_hebrew: יום... עת — the same day/time pair as v. 36 (ומהיום ההוא ומהעת ההיא) and the same two verbs the discourse has been built on: חכה (wait, v. 13) and ידע (know, vv. 36, 39, 42, 43). The Hebrew chapter is woven on repeated roots that the Greek renders with unrelated words, breaking the weave.

verses.translation: and he will separate him{H6504}, and will set{H7760} his portion{H2506} with the hypocrites{H2611}; there{H8033} will be weeping{H1065} and gnashing{H2786} of teeth{H8127}.

one_way_hebrew: חנף (H2611) — Job's word for the godless dissembler (Job 8:13; 13:16, 'a chanef shall not come before him'); Greek ὑποκριτής ('stage-actor') is the theater metaphor, חנף the covenant one.
חרק שינים — 'gnash teeth': Ps 35:16; 37:12 ('the wicked... gnasheth upon him with his teeth'); Lam 2:16. The idiom is the Psalter's.

ויפרידהו (H6504, parad) — 'separate him': the same verb as v. 41's separating of good from evil. Greek διχοτομήσει ('cut him in two') is a different and stranger picture; the Hebrew closes the chapter on ONE verb of separation used twice — the messengers separate the good from the evil (v. 41), and the master separates the false servant to his portion (v. 51).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (24:51): ויפרידהו] ויפחדהו A.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 24 in the Shem Tov Hebrew differs from the Greek at nearly every hinge of the discourse. (1) 24:29 reads 'And in that hour, AFTER THOSE DAYS, the sun will be darkened' — no 'immediately,' no 'tribulation'; mss ABEFG add צרת ('the tribulation of'), assimilating to the Greek, but the base text stands without it. The moon-clause quotes Isa 13:10 verbatim (והירח לא יגיה אורו). (2) 24:35 ends at 'the heavens and the earth will pass away' — no ms of the Shem Tov family carries 'but my words shall not pass away.' (3) 24:36 reads 'And FROM that day and FROM that time there is none who knows — not even the messengers of the heavens — except the Father alone': no 'neither the Son,' and the preposition is מן ('from'), not 'concerning' — read after v. 35, the knowledge runs out from the day heaven and earth pass. (4) 24:37 reads 'in the DAYS of the Son of Man,' agreeing with Luke 17:26 against Greek Matthew's 'parousia' (mss ABEF assimilate to ביאתו 'his coming'). (5) 24:31 gathers the chosen 'with a SHOFAR and a great voice... from the four winds of the heavens, from the end of the heavens unto their ends' — a mosaic of Isa 27:13, Zech 2:10, and Deut 30:4. (6) 24:33 puts the returning one 'at the GATES' (לשערים), not 'doors.' (7) 24:40-41 name the two in the field 'the one righteous and the other wicked,' and append the explanation that the messengers will remove the stumbling-blocks (cf. Matt 13:41) — being 'taken' (נלכד, captured as in a snare) is the fate of the wicked. (8) 24:3 names Petros, Yochanan, and Andreah asking 'opposite the Sanctuary,' as in Mark 13:3. (9) The text glosses its own Hebrew words for foreign readers — בשורה as evangeli (v. 14), the abomination as Antichristos (v. 15) — glosses that only make sense if the Hebrew is the native text and the Greek-Latin vocabulary the visitor. One-way Hebrew throughout: Dan 12:1 at v. 21, Deut 13:2-3 at v. 24, Gen 1:28 at v. 38, Ps 104:27 at v. 45, Hab 2:3 at v. 48, Prov 23:20-21 at v. 49. Shem Tov's own section divisions fall at vv. 1 (Perek 100), 27 (101), 37 (102), and 42 (103). Ms order places v. 25 after v. 26.
